deer.name: Deer
deer.flavor: Soft-eyed. Watching the treeline, not you. That is a mistake.
tells: [b]Won't strike first.[/b] It opens Skittish and only turns on you if cornered or pressed several turns running - safe to open aggressive.
[b]Falls into a rhythm.[/b] It tends to alternate defend and light attack. Two Observes and you own the pattern.
deer.read: Skittish-heavy, almost no Calm. Your teaching fight.

rabbit.name: Rabbit
rabbit.flavor: It is already looking for the way out. It was looking before you arrived.
tells: [b]Almost never commits.[/b] It dodges and waits; it does not fight. A wasted Claw into its Dodge is how you lose the kill.
[b]Fragile.[/b] The lowest HP in the forest - if you can land a clean hit, it folds fast. Pressure over patience.
rabbit.read: Skittish to the point of cowardice. The easiest read - and the easiest Blood to fumble.

fox.name: Fox
tells: [b]The forest's first liar.[/b] Its Feint reads Aggressive but is a bluff for your Guard. An Aggressive read from a fox is a question, not a fact - and a heavy read is the real thing.
[b]Deceives with its health.[/b] Fresh, it feints and probes; wounded, it slips to Dodge and waits. Blocking one of its strikes throws it off its next attack.
fox.read: Calm-heavy, deceptive. The animal that teaches you Observe isn't gospel.

stoat.name: Stoat
stoat.flavor: Small, quick, and entirely without fear of you.
tells: [b]Quick and evasive.[/b] Like a fox that never learned to lie - it slips your heavies and chips with light strikes, but it won't Feint.
[b]Thrown by a block.[/b] Guard one of its strikes and it hesitates to press the next turn.
stoat.read: Skittish and relentless. A fox without the bluff.

boar.name: Boar
boar.flavor: Low to the ground and utterly convinced it is dangerous.
tells: [b]Gores while it's healthy.[/b] Fresh, it presses with its tusks; wounded, it turns to digging and bluffing instead of committing.
[b]Digs only when hurt.[/b] Dig heals 3 but wastes a turn, and it won't dig near full health - so a digging boar is a bleeding boar; press it.
boar.read: Aggressive when strong, greedy and evasive when wounded.

wolf_cub.name: Wolf Cub
wolf_cub.flavor: It has the eyes of the pack, but not yet the patience.
tells: [b]All teeth, no craft.[/b] It presses with claws but hasn't learned the Bite - a wolf without its worst trick.
[b]Hunts weakness like its elders.[/b] It grows more aggressive when your Breath runs low.
wolf_cub.read: Aggressive and unrefined. A preview of the wolf to come.

lynx.name: Lynx
lynx.flavor: The branches above you have been empty for a long time. Or at least, you thought they were.
tells: [b]Opens with an ambush.[/b] Its first move each fight is a committed strike - expect aggression turn one and be ready to eat or block it.
[b]Presses your weakness.[/b] It grows more aggressive the moment your Breath runs low, and favours quick light strikes to chip you down.

razorback.name: Razorback
razorback.flavor: It's tusks have come in. Your scars remember what they are capable of.
tells: [b]Enraged when wounded.[/b] Below 40% HP its attacks deal +1. Finishing it is more dangerous than starting it - don't get sloppy on the last hit.
[b]The Charge announces itself.[/b] A Calm wind-up precedes its heavy Charge. Read the set, block or wait it out, punish the recovery.
razorback.read: Aggressive, with a Calm tell before the big hit. Reads shift toward danger as its HP drops.

stag.name: Stag
stag.flavor: It has weathered more winters than you, and it does not spook.
tells: [b]Plays a real game.[/b] It varies pace and mixes a Feint in - an Aggressive read can be a bluff. Treat it like a fight, not a hunt.
[b]Patient.[/b] It won't overcommit; it waits for you to make the opening. Manage your Breath for the long fight.
stag.read: Balanced and deceptive - measured aggression around stretches of Calm.

wolf.name: Wolf
wolf.flavor: It is not in a hurry. It has already decided how this ends. It is only waiting for you to agree.
tells: [b]Blocking cools its tempo.[/b] Successfully Guarding a wolf attack makes it less likely to attack next turn - a clean block is a small opening, not just defense.
[b]Hunts weakness with the Bite.[/b] It presses when your Breath is low. The Bite is cheap if it lands raw, expensive if you block it - so read it, block it, and drain its Breath.
wolf.read: Calm-heavy for its tier. It wants you to guess wrong, then drains your Breath when you do.

leadwolf.name: Lead Wolf
leadwolf.flavor: The pack's last leader was strong. This one is stronger.
tells: [b]Calm when cornered.[/b] Unlike lesser prey it does NOT get twitchy at low HP - it goes Calm and unreadable. The kill is the hardest read of the fight; don't autopilot the finisher.
[b]Reads you back.[/b] Fall into a predictable rhythm and it begins to anticipate your attacks. [i](Pending the enemy-memory system - on record, not yet live.)[/i]
leadwolf.read: Deceptive and Calm-heavy, worst exactly when it's nearly dead.

greaterstag.name: Greater Stag
greaterstag.flavor: The antlers have counted more winters than you will. It is not frightened of the dark. It is the reason other things are.
tells: [b]The full kit.[/b] It has a Light Attack and its Gore, plus a Dodge and a Feint - it varies pace, it lies, it defends. This is a fight, not a hunt.
[b]Calm when cornered.[/b] Regal and unreadable at low HP. Combined with its Feint, the endgame is a genuine guessing match.
greaterstag.read: Balanced and deceptive - the most complete non-boss in the forest.

bear.name: Bear
bear.flavor: Everything else in the forest moves out of its way. You are about to explain why.
tells: [b]Calm and enraged at the finish.[/b] Below 40% HP it stays Calm (unreadable) AND deals +1. The most dangerous phase is the one you thought was the victory lap - save a full block for it.
[b]A slow, heaving recovery.[/b] When the Bear is spent it slumps into a two-turn rest - a rare, wide-open window. Pour everything in before it heaves back up to full.
bear.read: Slow, Calm-heavy, brutal on contact. A patience fight - bleed its Breath, punish the long Rests, respect the finish.
